# What Should Be Checked Besides IMU/Engineer Calibration When Unitree G1 Continuously Sways Left-Right and Walks In a Straight Line?

> **Current answer:** The issue was ultimately traced to an outdated lab firmware; after updating, the author reported significant improvement. Therefore, when repeated calibration fails, it is essential to record and verify the controller/robot firmware version against the compatibility matrix, and decide whether to continue adjusting the IMU or pelvis parameters. The original post did not provide specific version numbers, so official documentation or Issue should be consulted for verification.

## Problem and symptoms

- Unitree G1 remote-controlled walking exhibits sudden left-right swaying, body tilt, and inability to walk straight.
- Clear left-right swaying, inability to walk straight, body tilt; adjustment of pelvis angle did not provide immediate effect.

## Environment

- Unitree G1 lab real machine, remote-controlled walking mode, device located near the calibration/holding frame.

## Priority diagnostics

- Repeated use of a horizontal level to calibrate IMU, and full-body motor calibration; subsequent verification of the lab firmware version.

## Possible causes

- Outdated lab firmware.

## Attempts

- Multiple IMU calibration, full-body motor calibration, and adjustment of pelvis angle.

## Effective fixes

- Upgraded G1 lab firmware version.

## Result

- The author noted that the firmware update improved the situation, but no quantitative data on linear error or sway amplitude was provided.

## Limitations

- No disclosure of old/new firmware version, upgrade steps, or whether the system was fully restored.

## Safety notes

- In case of severe swaying, stop free walking and complete firmware and calibration checks in a safe frame or protective area.

## Image and visual evidence

- Visible images show Unitree G1 located near the lab support/calibration frame, indicating the issue occurs in the real machine environment; the image does not display firmware version, calibration parameters, or logs, so the root cause cannot be confirmed from the picture.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to G1 cases where the symptom appears suddenly and repeated calibration fails; other models cannot be directly applied.
